title: Reproducing VeriBench on Smaller Models: Minimum Model Scale for Any Lean 4 Compilation

original_idea.body:
# Reproducing VeriBench on Smaller Models: Minimum Model Scale for Any Lean 4 Compilation

**Problem:** LLaMA-70B achieves 0% compilation on Lean 4 VeriBench tasks. Claude 3.7 Sonnet achieves 12.5%. The minimum model scale at which any Lean 4 compilation occurs — a capability emergence threshold — is not characterized for open models.

**Direction:** Test VeriBench subset (50 tasks) on 7B, 13B, 34B models from two open model families. Find the smallest model that achieves non-zero compilation rate. Characterize which tasks (easy/medium/hard) the smallest successful model can handle. Plot compilation rate vs. model size.

**Why it matters:** Identifying the capability emergence threshold for formal verification informs when this capability should appear in smaller deployable models. If the threshold is higher than current open models, on-device formal verification remains far off.

**Relevant context:** LLaMA-70B at 0% vs. Claude at 12.5% suggests a threshold between these scales. VeriBench's easy set provides tractable tasks for smaller models. This is a replication with scale variation.
